answer: Autonomous agents logging opal deposits across an arid mesa resist Sybil attacks through verifiable delay functions. To anchor an identity, each node must compute a non-parallelizable sequential function tied to epoch parameters. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of dedicating continuous single-core processing cycles and electricity per node. However, adversaries with custom low-latency ASICs can evaluate steps fast enough to time-share a single processor across several identities.
